reflection: Results are not visible in this run, so I rely on priors. Volatility-regime and MSFT/NVDA peer features were the most useful existing factors, so I extend those. I will try mean-reversion and regime-conditioned features, and design partners that pair a market-condition factor with an Apple relative move. Past lessons are generic because there is no data on how the earlier factors scored.

lessons.name: aapl_vol10_to_vol60_ratio
lessons.lesson: Vol regime ratio is related to the useful volatility factors, but the 60d denominator is slow and may be noisy; no result visible.

lessons.name: msft_return_zscore_20d
lessons.lesson: Standardizing MSFT's return largely duplicates MSFT_return_1d, so it adds little new information.

lessons.name: aapl_overnight_gap
lessons.lesson: Overnight gap is noisy and partly captured by the 1d return; may help only in high-vol years.

lessons.name: aapl_close_location_in_range
lessons.lesson: Close location can signal short-term reversal but is a weak single-day signal.

lessons.name: qqq_vol_ratio_5_20
lessons.lesson: Market vol ratio is a regime signal that may be informative only combined with Apple's own moves.

lessons.name: aapl_minus_msft_5d_relative
lessons.lesson: 5d relative strength vs MSFT overlaps with existing 5d returns and is weak.

lessons.name: aapl_close_location_avg_3d
lessons.lesson: Smoothing the close location reduces noise, but the signal is still weak.

lessons.name: aapl_minus_msft_5d_vol_scaled
lessons.lesson: Vol scaling normalizes across regimes, which may help across years, but the base signal is weak.

lessons.name: aapl_intraday_return
lessons.lesson: Intraday return mostly duplicates the 1d return, with some reversal information.

lessons.name: peer_dispersion_1d
lessons.lesson: Peer disagreement is a market-condition proxy that is unsigned and so weak alone.

lessons.name: aapl_volume_trend_signed
lessons.lesson: Signed volume interacts price and volume, but it is noisy and highly correlated with the 1d return.

lessons.name: qqq_trend_vs_aapl_gap_20d
lessons.lesson: 20d gap vs QQQ is largely a combination of existing 20d returns, so it adds little.

factors.name: aapl_minus_msft_5d_vol_scaled_z
factors.hypothesis: The raw spread has a regime-dependent scale; a 60d z-score normalizes it against its own history and captures stretched relative moves that mean-revert.

factors.name: qqq_vol_ratio_5_60_signed
factors.hypothesis: The vol ratio alone is unsigned; multiplying by QQQ's 5d direction separates panic selloffs, which tend to bounce, from calm rallies.

factors.name: aapl_range_expansion_z
factors.hypothesis: Range relative to its own 20d norm flags abnormal-volatility days, which often precede reversal or continuation depending on regime.

factors.name: aapl_drawdown_from_20d_high
factors.hypothesis: Distance below the recent high measures oversold state and may give a nonlinear mean-reversion signal that random forest can use.

factors.name: nvda_minus_qqq_3d_lead
factors.hypothesis: NVDA's leadership over the index combined with the QQQ vol state indicates risk appetite in tech, which may spill over into Apple.

factors.name: aapl_gap_vs_qqq_gap
factors.formula: subtract(safe_divide(subtract(AAPL_Open, lag(AAPL_Close, 1)), lag(AAPL_Close, 1)), safe_divide(subtract(QQQ_Open, lag(QQQ_Close, 1)), lag(QQQ_Close, 1)))
factors.hypothesis: Apple's overnight gap relative to QQQ's isolates Apple-specific news, and it complements the peer disagreement measure of market state.
